one_liner: Safe-Rust Wasm 3.0 interpreter with a wasmtime-shaped API; compiles modules about 90x faster than Wasmtime's Cranelift JIT.
what_it_does: A WebAssembly interpreter (no JIT) for modules that are compiled, run once and thrown away, such as LLM-generated code from mutually distrusting tenants. Its public API mirrors wasmtime 45.x (Engine, Store<T>, Module, Linker, func_wrap, sync and async host functions, fuel, epochs, ResourceLimiter, Trap/WasmBacktrace), so an embedder can switch with a Cargo package rename (`wasmtime = { package = "submilli-wasm", ... }`). It covers only the part of the API its authors' product uses. Component model, WASI and threads are not supported.
how_it_is_fast: Module::new does validation and lowering in one fused decode pass over the bytes (wasmparser underneath). Each internal op is written once into module-wide arenas as a fixed 16-byte op, with wide immediates in side pools and branch targets in a folded sidetable, so no second pass and no machine-code generation happens. The authors measure this at about 1.4x the raw wasmparser validation cost. Store::new allocates nothing, and the dispatch loop (`loop { match op }` over explicit operand and frame stacks) runs sync host calls inside the loop without suspending. Execution speed was deliberately traded away for this.
when_to_use: Modules that run exactly once or a handful of times, where JIT compile time (Cranelift took ~190 ms for a 4 MiB module per the README) is most of the cost.

Multi-tenant hosts running untrusted guests: the tree has no unsafe code (CI-gated), guest-reachable paths trap instead of panicking, and memory, stack, fuel, epochs and GC heap are bounded per Store.
Embedders already written against wasmtime's API, including async host functions, who want interpreter-class startup without rewriting their integration.

Guests compiled from GC languages or using exception handling: it claims full Wasm 3.0 (GC, try_table/exnref, tail calls, memory64, multi-memory, SIMD behind a feature) with zero skips on the upstream spec suite.
Small modules (tens to hundreds of KiB) with light compute, where its run-once total beats eager Wasmi and Wasmtime in its own benchmark (469 us vs 837 us vs 5.72 ms at sieve(1k)).
when_not_to_use: Compute-heavy guests or modules reused many times: its own table shows CoreMark 715 vs Wasmtime 36996 and Wasmi 3032, and sieve(1M) run-once 57.39 ms vs Wasmtime 7.23 ms and Wasmi 11.30 ms. In the wasmi-benchmarks suite its execution geomean is x83.39 behind the fastest runtime.

If startup is the only goal and you can live without GC and exceptions: Wasmi with lazy translation (x1.37), Wasm3 lazy (x2.77) and DLR wasm-interpreter (x10.95) all start faster than submilli-wasm (x18.08) on the same suite.

Host-call-heavy loops where the boundary dominates: ping x100k takes 3.52 ms vs 325.92 us for Wasmtime and 1.15 ms for Wasmi (about 35 ns vs 3.3 ns and 11.5 ns per call, derived from page data), even though the README calls the boundary cheap.
Memory density matters more than startup: fixed 16-byte ops take about 2x Wasmi's resident size (spidermonkey 31.0 MiB vs 16.5 MiB).
You need WASI, the component model, threads/atomics, custom-page-sizes or wasmtime APIs beyond the subset implemented. The project is experimental: first commit 2026-07-06, 4 stars, no issues filed.

integration.dependencies: wasmparser 0.252, anyhow, gimli 0.33 (DWARF backtraces), serde, postcard; async-trait with the optional `async` feature
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 2021 edition; no rust-version declared (the code uses Option::is_none_or, stable since Rust 1.82)
integration.platforms: any target Rust supports (pure safe Rust, no JIT, no platform-specific code); a wasm32 smoke build is mentioned in commits
integration.thread_safety: Engine is Arc-backed and Send + Sync; Store<T> is Send when T: Send and !Sync, with one execution at a time per store. Run many stores in parallel on one engine; wasm threads are not supported.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the same type and method names as wasmtime 45.x via a Cargo rename, but only the subset the authors' product uses; no WASI, component model or threads, and some Config knobs (async_stack_size, cranelift_opt_level) are accepted as no-ops

gotchas: The measured code is old: wasmi-benchmarks pins submilli-wasm 0.1.2 and its Cargo.lock resolves 0.1.3 (2026-08-09). crates.io's latest is 0.1.9 (2026-10-03) and the repo is at 0.1.10. Later versions added lazy module visits and other compile-path changes, so current startup may differ from the plotted x18.08.

Panic hardening is recent: 'fix(gc): return errors instead of panicking on layout and type-registry lookups' (2026-10-02) and 'Harden interpreter against invariant panics' (2026-10-06). Its own README says a panic takes down every tenant in the process, so older versions, including the benchmarked 0.1.3, had guest-reachable panics. Pin to the newest version for untrusted code.

Config::async_support defaults to on in Config::default() (unlike wasmtime), but the setter's doc comment says 'Off by default' and ARCHITECTURE.md says sync entry points panic once async is enabled. The wasmi-benchmarks adapter calls the sync API with the default config, so check behaviour rather than trusting the docs. The setter only exists with the `async` feature.

Backtraces are on by default and cost about 10% startup and 20% module RAM; Config::wasm_backtrace(false) turns them off. The wasmi-benchmarks adapter leaves them on, so the suite's startup figure is slightly conservative. The dispatch loop is generic over the Store<T> data type, so it monomorphizes in your crate once per store type.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over Wasmi, DLR wasm-interpreter, Fizzy, toywasm or tinywasm when you need Wasm GC plus exception handling and wasmtime's API (including async host functions) for untrusted run-once guests. Wasmi with lazy translation starts faster and executes about 4x faster, so it is the better choice whenever GC and exceptions are not required.
verified_claims_summary: In the Wasmi author's wasmi-benchmarks startup suite (criterion, Store::new plus Module::new plus instantiate of 7 modules from CoreMark to ffmpeg, AMD EPYC 7763, probably a GitHub Actions VM, bench profile with fat LTO and codegen-units=1, stable rustc of unrecorded version), submilli-wasm 0.1.3 reaches a geomean of x18.08 relative to the per-case fastest runtime. Wasmtime with Cranelift is at x1634.19 and Wasmer with Cranelift at x1484.15, about 90x and 82x slower (derived from page data); for example coremark takes 118.5 us vs 9.87 ms. This is an interpreter beating optimizing JITs on compile time only. Lazy interpreters still start faster, and V8 starts faster on the big modules.
status_note: Active (100 commits since 2026-07-06, last commit 2026-10-06) and Apache-2.0, but self-described as experimental and maintained by one product team with 4 stars and no external issues. Fine to adopt for its stated niche if you pin the latest version and test the wasmtime API subset you use.
